rows.note: For the changeable-temper sense, 情緒化 is the all-purpose choice for someone whose mood or reactions change easily.

example.english: They are very moody; the slightest thing can suddenly make them angry or happy.
example.traditional: 佢個人好情緒化，少少事都可以突然嬲或者開心。
example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 jan4 hou2 cing4 seoi5 faa3 siu2 siu2 si6 dou1 ho2 ji5 dat6 jin4 niu5 waak6 ze2 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use 黑口黑面 when the person is visibly sulky or giving others a bad-tempered expression, rather than simply feeling depressed.

example.english: They were moody at work today and did not feel like greeting anyone.
example.traditional: 佢今日返工黑口黑面，見到人都唔想打招呼。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam1 jat6 faan1 gung1 hak1 hau2 hak1 min6 gin3 dou2 jan4 dou1 m4 soeng2 daa2 ziu1 fu1

rows.note: Use 悶悶不樂 for the depressed, gloomy, or inwardly brooding side of moody, especially when no visible sulking is implied.

example.english: My son has been moody lately, and he will not say what is wrong.
example.traditional: 阿仔呢排成日悶悶不樂，問佢咩事又唔肯講。
example.jyutping: aa3 zai2 nei1 paai4 seng4 jat6 mun6 mun6 bat1 lok6 man6 keoi5 me1 si6 jau6 m4 hang2 gong2
